title: fix: DropShadowFilter SWF encoding — passes always 0 and hideObject uses wrong bit
description:
Two encoding bugs in packages/swf/src/filters.ts writeDropShadowFilter():

**Bug 1 — Quality/passes hardcoded to 0:**
The flags byte comment says 'bits 0-3: Passes = 0' — passes are always written as 0.
Ruffle's DropShadowFilterFlags has PASSES = 0b11111 (bits 0-4), and num_passes() returns bits 0-4 directly. A value of 0 means zero blur passes, producing a flat (unblurred) shadow instead of the expected soft drop shadow.

The DropShadowFilter model type in packages/core/src/engine/filters.ts has no 'quality' field. Both need fixing:
1. Add 'quality?: 1 | 2 | 3' field to DropShadowFilter interface (default 1).
2. Update defaultDropShadow() factory to include quality: 1.
3. Encode passes in writeDropShadowFilter(): flags |= (f.quality ?? 1) & 0x1f;

**Bug 2 — hideObject uses wrong bit (bit 4) instead of clearing CompositeSource (bit 5):**
Current code: flags |= 1 << 5 (always); if (f.hideObject) flags |= 1 << 4;
Ruffle reads hide_object() as !flags.contains(COMPOSITE_SOURCE) — i.e., the object is hidden when bit 5 is CLEAR, not when bit 4 is set.
Ruffle's DropShadowFilterFlags has no bit 4 field for DropShadow; bit 4 is undefined/reserved.

Fix: 
  - Only set CompositeSource (bit 5) when hideObject is FALSE (not always 1).
  - Remove the bit 4 (OnTop) assignment — that bit is not used by Ruffle for DropShadow.
  Corrected: if (!f.hideObject) flags |= 1 << 5; // CompositeSource = !hideObject

Verified against:
- ruffle/swf/src/types/drop_shadow_filter.rs: COMPOSITE_SOURCE = 1 << 5, PASSES = 0b11111
- ruffle/core/src/avm1/globals/drop_shadow_filter.rs: hide_object() = !COMPOSITE_SOURCE; default quality = 1
- ruffle/render/src/filters.rs: impotent() does NOT check DropShadow so 0-pass shadow won't be skipped, but renders incorrectly
